themes_detail.label: Encampment surge in Sunnyside
themes_detail.summary: Homeless encampment complaints spiked to 29 THIS WEEK—a 427% jump from the 5.5-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.62)—suggesting either a sudden influx of unhoused residents or rapid visible clustering in the district that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 29 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.5-per-week 8-week average (427% increase)
Z-score of 5.62 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Most acute spike among all categories tracked
reporting_angles: On-the-ground reporting: where are encampments clustering and why now?
Interview unhoused residents about what drove migration to Sunnyside this week
City response: has Parks Dept or NYPD engagement changed, or is the city unprepared for sudden increase?

themes_detail.label: Curb and sidewalk deterioration cluster
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 14 THIS WEEK (700% above the 1.8-per-week baseline), while sidewalk complaints hit 20 last week (264% above 5.5-per-week average), suggesting widespread pedestrian-infrastructure failures that may indicate deferred maintenance or storm damage.
evidence: Curb condition: 14 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8-per-week 8-week average (700% spike, z-score: 10.22)
Sidewalk condition: 20 complaints last week vs. 5.5-per-week average (264% spike, z-score: 4.47)
Both spikes occur in same 1-2 week window, suggesting common cause (weather, contractor work, or systemic DOT/DEP failure)
reporting_angles: Visual documentation: map the worst curb/sidewalk damage across Sunnyside and Woodside
DOT response: why the sudden surge and what's the repair timeline?
Accessibility angle: how are elderly and disabled residents navigating failing infrastructure?

themes_detail.label: Tree-planting demand explosion
themes_detail.summary: New tree requests skyrocketed to 4 last week versus a near-zero 0.1-per-week baseline (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72), the single largest proportional spike in the dataset, indicating either a coordinated community campaign or sudden recognition of canopy loss.
evidence: 4 tree-planting requests last week vs. 0.1-per-week 8-week average (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72—highest z-score in dataset)
Converges with long-standing CB budget priority requesting 'new or expanded park or amenity'
Community Board has repeatedly requested parks/recreation funding, suggesting latent demand
reporting_angles: Community organizing: is there a grassroots tree-planting movement emerging in Sunnyside?
Tree canopy gap: has the district experienced recent tree loss (storm, disease, removal)?
Parks Dept capacity: can NYC respond to sudden demand, or will this be another unfunded request?

themes_detail.label: Safety/construction complaints at sites
themes_detail.summary: BEST/Site Safety complaints surged to 3 last week from a 0.1-per-week baseline (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69), concurrent with 626 DOB building permits filed (419 alterations, 108 new buildings) over 90 days, suggesting construction-zone hazards or inadequate oversight.
evidence: BEST/Site Safety complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.1-per-week 8-week average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Heavy construction activity: 626 permits filed in 90 days (419 alterations, 108 new buildings, 15 demolitions)
Active major rezonings (21-31 46th Ave, 31-10 & 31-16 Hunters Point, 50-02 Queens Blvd) suggest ongoing development pressure
reporting_angles: Jobsite safety audit: inspect the most active construction zones for compliance and hazards
DOB enforcement: are inspectors keeping pace with the 626-permit filings?
Development intensity: how is rapid rezoning/construction reshaping neighborhood safety and character?

themes_detail.label: Smoking/vaping complaints uptick
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or vaping complaints rose to 11 last week from a 3.5-per-week baseline (214% increase, z-score: 5.67), marking the lowest-severity but statistically significant spike, possibly indicating residential frustration with indoor air quality or enforcement gaps.
evidence: 11 smoking/vaping complaints last week vs. 3.5-per-week 8-week average (214% increase, z-score: 5.67)
Concurrent with noise complaints (829 over 90 days, suggesting general residential quality-of-life concerns)
Suggests possible enforcement gap or shift in resident tolerance
reporting_angles: Enforcement check: is DOHMH/NYPD responding to secondhand smoke complaints?
Vaping surge: is there a youth vaping trend in Sunnyside schools or parks?
Resident sentiment: interview complainants on why smoking enforcement suddenly matters to them
